claims.text: The initial AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is pre-alloyed and spherical and is typical of powder used for metallic additive manufacturing of miniature components.
Resonant acoustic mixing can deposit nano-scale yttrium oxide onto AlCrFeNiSi powder particles.
The resonant-acoustic-mixing treatment produces a uniform nano-scale yttrium oxide coating.
Yttrium-oxide-coated powder can be consolidated by laser powder bed fusion.
The proposed treatment is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi components a few millimeters in size fabricated under moderate laser energy input, modest substrate preheating, and an inert atmosphere.
The dispersed nano-oxides act as heterogeneous nucleation sites during solidification.
Nano-oxide-assisted nucleation refines the grains in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The nano-oxide treatment produces a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
The nano-oxide coating modifies layer-deposition thermal profiles by reducing localized thermal gradients.
The nano-scale yttrium oxide dispersoids pin grain boundaries.
Reduced localized thermal gradients and grain-boundary pinning mitigate residual-stress buildup.
Dispersed yttrium oxide provides dispersion strengthening.
Coated-powder AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual stresses than components made from uncoated powder under conventional high-energy conditions.
Coated-powder AlCrFeNiSi components will have a finer and more uniform microstructure than the uncoated baseline.
Coated-powder AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit increased yield strength and ductility relative to the uncoated baseline.
The effectiveness of the intervention for larger geometries or substantially different additive-manufacturing conditions is unproven.

contradictions.description: The stated prediction compares coated powder processed at moderate energy with an uncoated high-thermal-load baseline, whereas the falsification experiment requires identical parameters and equivalent energy input for coated and uncoated powders. Thus, the experiment does not directly test the stated cross-regime comparison, and the stated comparison also confounds powder treatment with processing energy.
